title: allowlist policy (CAM-102): AC de hand-file-via-/cam-issue deve ser reviewer-verified, nao worker-implemented
description: No CAM-162, o AC13 pedia que a cerimonia de operador fosse hand-filada via /cam-issue pelo ORQUESTRADOR antes do ship. O worker de US-004 satisfez o AC criando scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0164.json DIRETO no working tree -- o hook orch-agent-allowlist bloqueia spawn de Task/Agent mas NAO bloqueia Write de arquivo. Isso colidiu (add/add) com o CAM-0164 que eu filei via cam issue --file-local, forcando resolucao de conflito manual no ship. Correcao: (a) o hook/policy deveria impedir o worker de escrever em scripts/cam/issues/ (so o orquestrador filra, via cam issue), e/ou (b) ACs de tipo 'hand-file via /cam-issue' devem ser verificados pelo reviewer (checar que o issue existe no main), nunca implementados pelo worker escrevendo o arquivo. Vincula CAM-102 (refino do allowlist). P3.

acceptanceCriteria: The worker-actor Write-deny in orch-agent-allowlist.sh (gated on CAM_WORKER set AND CAM_SESSION set) DENIES Write/Edit/MultiEdit to any file path under scripts/cam/issues/ (the whole directory), in addition to the existing scripts/cam/prd.json deny.

The single hard-coded suffix check is converted to a small structured deny-set (case/loop over the two protected suffixes: *scripts/cam/prd.json and *scripts/cam/issues/*); intent reads as 'worker-protected cam control-plane state'.
The pre-existing prd.json worker Write-deny still holds (no regression), verified by the existing cases in test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts.
A worker Write to a path OUTSIDE cam control-plane state (e.g. under src/) remains ALLOWED.
A planner Write (CAM_SESSION set, CAM_WORKER unset) to scripts/cam/issues/ or prd.json remains ALLOWED; an unscoped session (CAM_SESSION unset) is fully unrestricted.

The deny logic is identical across all three synced copies: .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, templates/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, and the src/vendor/_generated.ts embed (regenerated by the build).
New test cases in test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts exercise the scripts/cam/issues/ deny path (worker DENY, planner ALLOW, unscoped ALLOW) by spawning the real hook script.

subagent-planner.md carries an explicit rule (next to the existing requires:'operator' rule): a 'hand-file issue via /cam-issue' requirement is NEVER a worker implementation story; it is encoded as a file-assert oracle acceptance criterion that verifies the issue exists on main (e.g. git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json), which the reviewer's existing behavioral gate re-runs.

No new reviewer behavioral-gate code is added; the (b) fix reuses the existing file-assert oracle mechanism (optionally one clarifying line in subagent-reviewer.md that on-main existence checks are legitimate oracle targets).
spec.scope: Close the CAM-162 add/add collision class by hardening the worker-vs-orchestrator control-plane boundary along two layers. (a) Mechanical: extend the CAM-63 worker-actor Write-deny hook (orch-agent-allowlist.sh) so the worker actor (CAM_WORKER) is denied Write/Edit/MultiEdit to scripts/cam/issues/ as well as scripts/cam/prd.json, converting the single suffix conditional into a small structured deny-set, across all three synced hook copies plus tests. (b) Process: add planner guidance that a hand-file-via-/cam-issue requirement is expressed as an on-main file-assert oracle acceptance criterion (verified by the reviewer's existing behavioral gate), never handed to a worker to satisfy by writing the file on-branch. Out of scope: any new reviewer behavioral-gate machinery, a brittle planner-output unit test, or protecting paths beyond prd.json + issues/.
gotchas: Dual-copy is per-file (lesson CAM-123): the hook lives in .claude/hooks/, templates/.claude/hooks/, and is embedded in src/vendor/_generated.ts; all three must carry the same deny logic and the build regenerates _generated.ts.

The deny is keyed on CAM_WORKER=1 (set only on the implementer spawn path, not the shared workerEnvPrefix used by reviewer/planner) plus CAM_SESSION; it must NOT block the planner (writes prd.json legitimately) nor the orchestrator (files issues on main via cam issue).

file_path arrives absolute in production, so match by suffix/glob; block the whole scripts/cam/issues/ directory (*scripts/cam/issues/*), since the CAM-162 collision was the ADD of a new CAM-0164.json there.
Hook is fail-closed when jq is absent; preserve that.

Planner guidance is prompt-only: no planner-output unit test (an LLM prompt assertion would be brittle); the mechanical (a) guard is the real enforcement, (b) is guidance leaning on the file-assert oracle path.
